intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic (including compound heterozygous) mutation in the RAB34 gene.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is caused by biallelic mutation in the RAB34 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families. Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34)
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic RAB34 variants cause the novel OFDS.

checks.claim: Biallelic RAB34 mutations causing OFD20 include compound heterozygous mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype and compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper does report compound heterozygous variants, but it describes the condition as an atypical skeletal ciliopathy rather than OFD20.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is a ciliopathy in which defects in development of the face and oral cavity occur together with digit anomalies. Bruel et al. (2023) reported that it was accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal, and anorectal defects. Batkovskyte et al. (2024) described an affected fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype that included cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and both pre- and postaxial polydactyly.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is a ciliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Pathogenic variants in over 20 genes encoding ciliary proteins have been found to cause OFDS through deleterious structural or functional impacts on primary cilia. We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34
checks.explanation: OFDS-RAB34 is caused by a ciliary gene and impairs cilium assembly, so it is a ciliopathy.

checks.claim: In OFD20, defects in development of the face and oral cavity occur together with digit anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: Oral-facial-digital syndromes (OFDS) are a group of clinically and genetically heterogeneous disorders characterized by defects in the development of the face and oral cavity along with digit anomalies.
checks.explanation: OFD20 is a form of OFDS, which the paper defines this way.

checks.claim: Bruel et al. (2023) reported that OFD20 was accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal, and anorectal defects.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) described a fetus affected with OFD20 who had an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype and compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper does describe a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy, but it does not label the fetus as having OFD20.

paragraphs.text: Batkovskyte et al. (2024) reported a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy phenotype. The fetus had multiple malformations, among them posterior neck edema, micrognathia, small low-set ears, auricular hypoplasia, cleft lip and palate, short extremities, and an uncommon combination of preaxial and postaxial polydactyly. A sib of the fetus was unaffected.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of OFD20 is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Bruel et al. (2023) found biallelic RAB34 variants in affected individuals. Batkovskyte et al. (2024) found compound heterozygous variants in an affected fetus: one variant was inherited from each parent, and the unaffected sib carried only the paternal variant.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of OFD20 is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by exome sequencing bi-allelic missense variants in a novel disease-causing ciliary gene RAB34 in four individuals from three unrelated families.
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic variants suggest recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not state the inheritance pattern or describe segregation of the variants.

paragraphs.text: Using exome sequencing in 4 individuals with OFD20 from 3 unrelated families, Bruel et al. (2023) identified biallelic missense mutations in the RAB34 gene. RAB34 encodes a Rab GTPase that mediates ciliary membrane formation and acts selectively in cell types that use the intracellular ciliogenesis pathway. The mutations clustered near the C terminus of RAB34. Functional studies showed that the mutant proteins had a strong loss of function. Some mutant proteins could still be recruited to the mother centriole, but cells expressing mutant RAB34 had a significant defect in cilium assembly.

paragraphs.text: In a fetus with an atypical skeletal ciliopathy, Batkovskyte et al. (2024) used genome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous variants in the RAB34 gene. The maternally inherited variant was a c.254T-C transition causing an ile85-to-thr (I85T) substitution, and the paternally inherited variant was a c.691C-T transition causing an arg231-to-ter (R231X) substitution. The unaffected sib carried only the paternal variant. The authors noted that Rab34-null mice show a ciliopathy phenotype with cleft palate and polydactyly, which they took as support for pathogenicity.

agent.process_note: Both papers are abstract only, and I read both abstracts in full. Bruel et al. (2023) does not name individual variants or say whether they were homozygous or compound heterozygous; it says only 'bi-allelic missense'. So the only allelic variants listed are the 2 from Batkovskyte et al. (2024). No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the RAB34 MIM number and chromosomal location. I inferred autosomal recessive inheritance from biallelic variants and parental segregation; neither abstract states it explicitly. Neither abstract gives ancestry, consanguinity, ages, or details of individual patients.
